turns.doctor_question: Hello. What brings you into the clinic today?
turns.patient_response:
Well, I came because... it's my husband’s sister. She’s been working this family business angle so she can get control of the money and push me out of all the decisions. Which, honestly, doesn't surprise me one bit. She’s always been like that, just flashy and wanting to be the center of attention. 

Like this one time years ago, she bought this bright yellow car. Who buys a yellow car? It just shows all the dirt. We lived near the old limestone quarry back then, and I used to tell my husband that the dust would ruin the paint on that thing in a month. The dust was just terrible out there, coating the front windows every single morning. I had to wash them with vinegar and newspaper. My grandmother taught me that trick. Works better than Windex, I swear. You don't get those streaks when the sun hits it in the afternoon... 

But, um... what was I saying? Oh, right, his sister. People in the family keep trying to smooth it over, telling me I'm getting worked up over nothing, but I know what I’ve been seeing for more than a year now. She's trying to push me out. Oh, and speaking of the windows, I need to remember to pick up more vinegar on the way home, actually. The store on 4th street has it cheaper than the big supermarket.

symptom_reasoning.S019: The patient expresses a fixed, persecutory belief that her sister-in-law is plotting to take control of the family money and push her out, maintaining this conviction despite family members telling her she is getting worked up over nothing.
symptom_reasoning.S021: The patient exhibits tangentiality and derailment in her speech, wandering from the topic of her sister-in-law to a yellow car, a limestone quarry, and washing windows with vinegar, eventually losing her train of thought.

turns.doctor_question: Lately, have you found that you need much less sleep than usual to feel rested?
turns.patient_response:
Less sleep? No, I don't think so. I still need my regular eight hours, or I'm just dragging the whole next day. I've always been like that, though. I have to get my rest. 

It can be hard sometimes, though, because my husband snores like an absolute freight train. I actually had to start buying those little foam earplugs. You know the ones? They come in that big plastic jar at the pharmacy. I always get the bright orange ones. I tried the blue ones once, but they were way too stiff and made my ears ache terribly in the morning. It’s funny how they charge you more for the blue ones just because they say "advanced" on the box, but they’re actually worse. Just like that memory foam pillow I bought off the TV last year. They promised it would stay cool all night, but it felt like sleeping on a hot brick. I ended up giving it to the dog. He loves it, though... he drags it right into the middle of the living room rug every afternoon. 

Um, but anyway... what were you asking me? Oh, right, my sleep. Yeah, no, I sleep just the regular amount. I definitely haven't noticed needing any less of it.

symptom_reasoning.S008: The patient demonstrates distractibility by unrelated thoughts, going on a long tangent about earplugs, pillows, and her dog before losing her train of thought and forgetting the doctor's question.
symptom_reasoning.S036: The patient explicitly denies needing less sleep, stating she still needs her regular eight hours to avoid dragging the next day.

turns.doctor_question: Have you ever heard sounds or voices when there was no one around or that other people couldn't hear?
turns.patient_response:
Voices? No, I don't hear anything like that. Just the normal sounds, you know? Like the house settling, or the refrigerator humming. 

Actually, speaking of the refrigerator, ours has been making this awful rattling noise for about three weeks now. It's one of those stainless steel ones with the ice maker in the door. I told my husband we should have just gotten a plain white one, because the stainless shows every single fingerprint. Every time my nephew comes over, he leaves these sticky little handprints right near the handle. He loves grape jelly, that kid. He'll eat a grape jelly sandwich for breakfast, lunch, and dinner if you let him. I tried making him one with strawberry jam once, the kind with the seeds in it? He took one bite and spit it right into the kitchen sink. Took me twenty minutes to rinse it all down the drain. You have to be careful with those older pipes, you know, they get clogged so easily. The plumber we had out last spring said our pipes are probably original to the house, which means they're from the sixties. 

But, um... wait, what were we talking about? Oh, voices. Right. No, no voices or anything like that. Just the regular noises.

symptom_reasoning.S021: The patient exhibits tangentiality and loose associations, wandering from the topic of the refrigerator to fingerprints, her nephew, jelly, plumbing, and the 1960s before losing her train of thought.
symptom_reasoning.S020: The patient explicitly denies hearing voices or sounds that aren't there, stating she only hears normal noises.

turns.doctor_question: Do you generally find it hard to trust people in your life, or is this issue mainly just with your sister-in-law?
turns.patient_response:
Well, no, it's really just her. I don't have trouble trusting people in general. I still keep up with all my normal things, you know? Like my quilting group, choir practice, my GED lessons, and my senior walks. I still do all of that just like I always have. 

Actually, at my GED classes—I'm trying to finally get my diploma, you know, since I never finished high school—we were just doing fractions last week. Math is just... well, it's something else. The teacher was talking about dividing things into sevenths. Who cuts anything into sevenths? If I bake a pie, I cut it into eight pieces. It just makes sense. I made a rhubarb pie for the church bake sale last month, and I had to use this new store-brand tin foil because they were out of the heavy-duty kind. It was so flimsy, it tore right down the middle when I tried to cover the edges of the crust. I hate when that happens. You try to use what they have, and it just ruins the bake. The edges got a little too brown, but people still bought it anyway. Mrs. Gable bought two slices, and she's usually so picky about her sweets. 

Um... wait, what was I saying? Oh, right, trusting people. Yeah, so I still go to all my normal groups and talk to everyone just fine. The issue is really just with my husband's sister. That's what's changed—mostly just how much I trust her, and I guess which family gatherings I actually feel comfortable going to anymore. If I know she's going to be there trying to run the show and scheme, I'd just rather stay home.

symptom_reasoning.S025: The patient explicitly denies losing interest or withdrawing socially, stating she still attends her quilting group, choir practice, and other activities just as she always has.
symptom_reasoning.S072: The patient denies having generalized negative beliefs or trust issues with people, stating her lack of trust is specifically limited to her sister-in-law.
symptom_reasoning.S075: The patient denies feeling detached from others in general, noting she still goes to her groups and talks to everyone just fine.
